terra.problem: “Wrong century for the Pharisees” is unsupported and inaccurate. The Pharisees appear in the first century, as does Revelation.
The explanation identifies “them” as the people holding those teachings, but the text does not explicitly identify the referent.
The explanation treats the identity of “them” and the reason repentance comes first as explicit, though the text does not state either.
The text says the stone bears a new name known only to its recipient. It does not say nobody else can peek at the stone.
Exodus 31:18 describes stone tablets but does not identify what was written on them as the Ten Commandments. The cited reference does not establish the stated fact.
“It’s between Jesus and the one who gets the stone” adds that Jesus knows the name, while the passage says it is known only to the recipient.
“They’re doing more now” turns greater deeds into a claim about quantity. The passage does not say there are more deeds.
Jesus tells Ephesus it has abandoned its first love, not that its latest deeds are weaker than its first. The explanation treats those as the same comparison.
“They’re doing more now” claims a greater quantity of deeds, while the passage says only that the latest deeds are greater.
The passage says Jezebel is unwilling to repent. It does not establish that she never repents later; it simply does not report a later repentance.
The passage says Jesus searches minds and hearts. It does not say He does not look at how long a church has existed.
“That’s why Papa keeps the ovens warm” refers to Papa Dorin in the third person. He talks about himself as “I.”
